paradise: burn 2018-2019 (-0.227 NDVI), across most of the area (73%)

false_positives_reviewed.lake-mead water_loss 2021-2022: Real: Lake Mead's record low was 2022. Outside the gold window (2000-2015 +-2), so the scorer counts it as a false positive.
false_positives_reviewed.palm-jumeirah water_loss 2012-2024: Real: the frames show new reclaimed land on the east side (Dubai Harbour) between 2012 and 2024. Not in the gold list.
false_positives_reviewed.summerlin other/built_frac: Real change, wrong kind: see weaknesses (desert soil counts as built).

missed.lake-mead water_gain 2023: 2023-2024 is only ~0.03 above the single low year 2022 and falls back by 2026; against a 3-year window it is not a rise at all. No sensible penalty makes a 2-year, 2-sigma bump a level change without also firing on the control.
missed.summerlin urban_growth: Detected, but as other/built_frac -0.73: bare desert passes the built_frac test (NDBI > 0, NDVI < 0.2), so the area read 100% 'built' in 1984 and building a city with lawns LOWERED it. Following the README mapping (built falls -> other) gives the wrong kind. This is a metric-definition problem, best fixed in the contract (e.g. a bare-soil exclusion, like schema 1.1's water exclusion), not with a detector hack.
missed.willow-run x3 (demolition 2014-15, test: Each is ~1% of the 36 km2 square. built_frac noise there is sigma 0.011 with single-year dips (1992, 2014, 2023) of 0.03-0.04, so a 1% step is below both the physical minimum (3%) and 3 sigma. Not visible in an area-wide series at 6 km.
missed.delray urban_growth 2019-2024 (bridge): Same: the bridge and port of entry are a small share of the square and built_frac noise is sigma 0.020 (haze, Detroit summers).

method.segmentation: ruptures PELT, model='l2' (mean shift), min_size=3 years, jump=1, run separately on ndvi_mean, water_frac, built_frac.
method.penalty: pen = 2 * sigma^2 * ln(n) (BIC for a mean shift in Gaussian noise), sigma = 1.4826 * MAD(first differences) / sqrt(2), floored at 0.005 / 0.002 / 0.003 (ndvi / water / built) because flat, 4-decimal series would otherwise give sigma ~ 0. Scaling by each series' own sigma is what lets one rule serve a noisy city and a calm lake.
method.merging: Back-to-back shifts in the same direction merge into one gradual change if the pause between them is <= 5 years (PELT cuts a ramp into steps). start_year = last year of the old level, end_year = first year of the new level; magnitude = mean(new level segment) - mean(old level segment).

MIN_JUMP.why: NDVI 0.05 ~ healthy vs stressed canopy, beyond sun-angle/phenology spread; 2-3% of the area ~ 0.7-1.1 km2 of a 6 km square, visible in the film. built gets more room because its NDBI test is the noisiest.

MIN_JUMP_SIGMAS.why: 43 years of noise: 2 sigma would fire by chance on the control.

MIN_SEGMENT_YEARS.why: A 2-year level can be one hazy summer plus a neighbour; with 2, the control fires (Central Park water 1986-87).

MIN_PERSISTENCE.why: FR-22; persistence_years = consecutive years from end_year that stay nearer the new level than the old. Burns exempt.

region_pixel_threshold.why: Per-pixel means over up to 3 years each side. NDVI 0.15 ~ 2.5x the control's per-pixel flicker (0.06, ADR-002); for water/built the pixel's class flipped in most window years.

MIN_REGION_SHARE.why: Largest 8-connected changed area must be >= 0.5% of the square (~0.18 km2, ~200 pixels): a real change is one place, not salt-and-pepper.

MIN_EXPLAINED_SHARE.why: That area must hold >= 20% of the whole per-pixel change. A sensor/haze/phenology shift moves every pixel a little, so its largest area holds ~1-7% (control 2%, Paradise burn-scar 'built' rise 7%, Palm diffuse greening 3%, Summerlin greening 1%); real changes hold 28-90%.

burn.why: Large NDVI drop, >= 70% of it in one year, and the changed area's median dNBR (NIR vs SWIR2) >= 0.27, the USGS moderate-low severity class.

thresholds.shrinking_lake_rule: A built_frac rise whose changed pixels were >= 50% water in the before window is exposed shore / reclaimed land: dropped if a water_loss already covers those years, otherwise relabelled water_loss. Never urban_growth.
thresholds.burn_scar_rule: A built_frac rise in the same years as a burn whose changed pixels lie >= 50% inside the burn area is the scar (burnt ground passes the built test): dropped.
thresholds.DR-6: Each year gets an instrument family (OLI if L8/L9 present, else TM if L4/L5, else ETM+ = L7-only). A switch year is one whose family differs from the previous kept year. Flag if start or end year is within 1 year of a switch.

method.ranking: Largest first by |magnitude| / MIN_JUMP[metric], so metrics in different units compare fairly. At most 5 (HL-2).

sensitivity.note: Changing one knob at a time, counts per place (lake, paradise, summerlin, palm, central-park, ypsilanti, willow, delray), baseline 3/1/1/2/0/0/0/0.
sensitivity.penalty_factor_1_or_4: no change: the size, noise and region tests decide, not the penalty
sensitivity.MIN_EXPLAINED_SHARE_0: paradise +1 (burn scar as urban_growth would survive the region-size test only), control still 0
sensitivity.MIN_SEGMENT_YEARS_2: control 1, palm +1, summerlin +1, willow +1: the main guard against 2-year blips
sensitivity.MIN_REGION_SHARE_0: no change (explained-share test catches the same cases)

tried: min_size=2 and merging any same-direction run: Lake Mead became one 2000-2022 change, Palm one 2002-2020 change, Willow Run/Ypsilanti a 1985-2013 'vegetation_gain' ramp, and the control produced 3 changes (built 1986-1998 +0.12, two water blips).
Pause limit for merging (5 years) and min_size=3: removed the long drift ramps and the control's blips.
Burn-scar rule by 'changed pixels were green (NDVI >= 0.4) before': failed on Paradise (houses/roads in the forest are mixed pixels). Replaced by 'changed pixels lie inside the burn area'.
Region-coherence tests: largest-area size alone missed some diffuse cases; adding the explained-share test cleanly split real (>= 0.28) from drift (<= 0.07).
Looked at frames: Summerlin 1988 vs 2014 (desert -> suburb with golf courses), Palm Jumeirah 2012 vs 2024 (new Dubai Harbour land on the east side).
weaknesses: Recall 3/9 is far below the 80% bar. Four misses (Willow Run x3, Delray) are changes of ~1% of the square under 2-3% series noise: no series-based detector at 6 km will see them without lowering thresholds to where the control fires. They need a per-pixel detector run directly on the composites, or a smaller area.
Summerlin is detected with the wrong kind because built_frac counts bare desert as built. Needs a contract-level metric fix (agreed with Vanessa), not a detector rule.
Short changes (Lake Mead's 2023 rebound) are invisible by design: min_size=3 and 3 sigma.
Gradual changes are cut at 5-year plateaus, so Lake Mead's decline is 3 separate water_loss changes instead of one 2000-2022 story; the agent must stitch them.
The burn kind relies on dNBR; a clear-cut also passes. Burns are only detected on ndvi_mean, so a fire in a scrubby, low-NDVI area (< 0.10 drop) becomes vegetation_loss.
The lon/lat bbox maps pixel extents linearly onto place.bbox (the composite is a UTM square), so edges can be off by a pixel or two.
8-connected BFS in pure Python is ~0.1-0.3 s for large masks (Paradise 73%); fine for <2 s but the slowest part.
Tuned and checked on 8 places only; the explained-share gap (0.07 vs 0.28) is wide but rests on few examples.

dependency.timing_note: 0.5-0.65 s max per place in repeated runs; one run hit 1.49 s while other spike agents were loading the machine.
dependency.note: Python 3.12 wheel installed cleanly on Windows. Only rpt.Pelt(model='l2') is used: about 20 lines of dynamic programming that could be written in numpy if the extra dependency is not wanted.
